full_judgment:
Farid Ahmed J : This appeal at the instance of the plaintiffs has been preferred against the judgment and decree dated 25-2-2007 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 163 of 2002 dismissing the suit.

2. The appellant as' plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid Title Suit No. 163 of 2002 for declaration that the mortgage deed and power of attorney mentioned in 'kha' schedule of the plaint in respect of 'ka' schedule property are collusive, forged, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs and that they are 16 annas owner of the suit property and for further declaration that-the preliminary decree dated 27-9- 2000 and the final decree dated 25-3-2001 passed by the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj, in Attha Rin Suit No. 59 of 1993 are also illegal, collusive, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

3. The case of the plaintiff-appellants are that:

The land measuring 0.32 decimal of CS Plot No. 183 and CS Khatian No. 96 of Mouza Khanpur, PS Fatullah, District-Narayangonj along with other lands belonged to Manu as raiyati right; that Manu died leaving 2 sons namely Abdul Kader and Kudrat Ullah and only daughter Haytun Bewa; that thereafter Abdul Kader died leaving 2 sons Abdul Gani and Ali Hossain and they became owner of the land of their father as his heirs and successors; that Hay tun Bewa had transferred her share in the suit land along with other lands to Abdul Gani and Ali Hossain through registered deed being No. 1162 dated 31-1-1946 and that these Abdul Gani and Ali Hossain had acquired 1.128 acres of land by way of purchase and inheritance; that while Abdul Gani had been in possession of 0.564 acre of land in the aforesaid CS Khatian No. 96 he died leaving Mobarak Hossain, Asrafuddin, Nuruddin, Shafiuddin and defendant No.5, Akhiluddin as 5 sons and Sahera Begum, Jahanara Begum and Hena Begum as 3 daughters; that during SA operation the name of the heirs of Abdul Gani were recorded along with the name of heirs of Manu and SA Khatian No. 156 was correctly prepared; that in the said Khatian the name of Nazimuddin and Alimuddin were recorded as sons of Abdul Gani but in fact they were not the sons of Abdul Gani; that Ali Hossain, Mobarak Hossain, Asrafuddin Ahmed and Nuruddin Ahmed had transferred 0.37 acres of land of plot No. 183 to one Shahbuddin Miah through registered deed No. 1950 dated 8-3-1963 and delivered possession to him; that while Shahbuddin Miah had been in possession of entire 3'7 decimal of land of CS Plot No. 183 including other lands of other plots, he had transferred the said land to one Iman Ali and his sister Gedi Bibi vide registered deed No. 2696 dated 7-5-1965, that while aforesaid Iman Ali and Gedi Bibi had been in possession of the said land for more than 12 years Gedi Bibi died leaving his brother Iman Ali and her share in the suit land devolved upon her brother and while Iman Ali became the owner of said 0.37 acre of land of suit plot No. 183, he again transferred 5 decimal of land to plaintiff No. 8 through registered deed being No. 8776 dated 8-7-1976; that plaintiff No. 8 mortgaged the suit property with the Bangladesh Krishi Bank; Fatullah Branch; that Iman Ali also had transferred 0.04 and 1/4 acre of land to Mosammat Suraiya Begum vide registered deed No. 8801 dated 17-12-1981; and on the same date he further had transferred 0.06 and 1/4acre of land to Mosammat Jesmin Akter@ Layla, Most. Najnin Akter @ Dipali, Most. Nasrin Akter & Shamoli and Shahinur Islam vide registered deed being No. 8802 dated 17-12-1981; that Iman Ali also had transferred 0.04 and 1/4 acre of land to Suraiya Begum vide kabala deed No. 8778 dated 15-12-1981; he further transferred 0.06 and 1/4 acre of land to Jesmin Akter and others vide registered deed No. 43 dated 4-1-1982 and on the same date he also transferred 0.06 acre of land to Md Anower Uddin vide registered deed No. 44 and thus the purchasers became owners and possessors of 0.32 acre of land of CS Plot No. 183; that while Anower Uddin, Most Suraiya Begum, Most. Jesmin Akter, Nasrin Akter, Most. Najnin Akter and Md Shahinur Islam had been in possession of 0.27 acres of land of CS plot No. 183, Most Jesmin Akter @ Layla and Most. Najnin Akter @ Dipali had transferred 0.05 acre of land to plaintiff No.1, Most. Rowshan Ara Beguinfrom CS Plot No. 183 corresponding to RS Plot No. 259 vide registered deed No. 5899 dated 5-7-1986; that on the same date Md Anoweruddin had transferred 0.06 acre of land to Kazi Sharif Ahmed from the aforesaid suit plot vide registered deed No. 5900; that Most. Suraiya Begum further transferred 0.04 and 1/4 acre of land to plaintiff No.1 vide registered deed No. 7415 dated 28-12- 1988; on the same date she further had transferred 0.04 and 1/4acre of land to Kazi Sharif Ahmed vide deed No. 7416; that Most. Suraiya Begum further transferred 0.0750 acre of land of aforesaid CS Plot No. 183 to Kazi Sharif Ahmed on being appointed as guardian of her minor children Nasrin Akhter and Shahinur Islam through case No. 53 of 1987 of the 2nd Court of Joint District Judge, Narayangonj vide deed No. 1233 dated 18-3-1991; that Kazi Sharif Ahmed became owner of 0.1775 decimal ofland and Rowshan Ara Begum became owner of 0.0925 acre of land and separate mutation khatian were prepared in their respective names; thereafter they dug pond and constructed houses by filling earth on their purchased land; they also took electricity and gas connection and they lived in the said houses with their family members and also possessed the same through different tenants and, enjoying usufructs from the trees; that Kazi Sharif Ahmed died leaving wife plaintiff No. 1 and 6 sons plaintiff Nos. 2-7 and 0.1775 acre of land of Kazi Sharif Ahmed devolved upon the plaintiffs by inheritance and also by purchase; that plaintiff Nos. 1-7 became owner of 0.27 acre of land; they mutated their names; separate joma was also prepared in their names and that they had been in possession of the said land for more than 12 years within the knowledge of defendant Nos. 3- 7; that during RS operation the land of CS Plot No. 183 corresponding to RS Plot No. 259 was correctly prepared in the name of Iman Ali predecessor in interest of the plaintiff Nos. 1-7 in RS and SA khatian; that the plaintiffs had been in possession of their 0.32 acres of land; that defendant No.5 have/had no right, title and interest in any part of the plaintiffs 0.32 acres of land; on the 1st week of May plaintiff No.2 came to know that defendant No.1, Bank has taken all steps to sell the suit property in auction; that after search in the Court of Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat defendant No, 2 came to know that defendant No. 4 in the name of his business enterprise (defendant No.3) mortgaged the suit property to defendant 'No.1, Bank and that defendant No. 1 obtained decree on 27-9-2000 in Artha Rin Suit No. 59 of 1893 against defendant Nos. 3 and 4 for realization of the loan money for an amount of Taka 23,52,402 and final decree was obtained on 25-3-2001; that plaintiffs thereafter filed an application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the Artha Rin Adalat for releasing their property from attachment and the said application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of2002; the learned Joint District Judge after hearing by his judgment and order dated 26-10-2002 rejected the said application; that from the plaint of Artha Rin Suit No. 59 of 1993 the plaintiffs came to know that defendant Nos. 3 and 4 took loan of Taka 39,50,000 and that as security of the said loan defendant No.5 mortgaged 0.33 acre of land of suit plot No. 183 in favour of defendant No. 1 on 21-11-1991; that defendant No.5 had no authority to mortgage the suit property to defendant No. I; that the plaintiffs and their predecessor-in-interest purchased the suit property from lawful owner and they are the heirs and successors of Abdul Gani who became owner of the suit property by purchase through the deed of the year 1963;that plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit property for more than 40 years; that the cause of action of the suit arose from 1st week of May, 2002 and on 18-5-2002 when the defendant No.1 obtained preliminary decree on 27- 9-2000 and final decree on 25-3-2001 and lastly on 26-10-2002 when the Artha Rin Adalat rejected their Misc. Case No. 17 of 2002.

4. By amending the plaint the plaintiffs stated that Md Akhiluddin predecessor of defendant Nos. 5(ka)-5(Uma) along with 6 others filed partition Suit No. 23 of 1996 for partition of their L88 acres of land including 0.37 acres of land of CS Plot No. 183 and that in the partition suit Md Akhiluddin Ahmed claimed saham of 0.07 and 3/5 acre of land of CS Khatian No. 96 and thus the mortgage of 0.33 acre of land by Md. Akhiluddin did not arise while he had no right, title and interest over 0.33 acre of land of suit plot No. 183.

5. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the 'suit by filing written statement denying all material allegations made in the plaint and their definite cases are that:

6. One Manu was the original owner of 0.37 acres of land of CS Plot No. 183; that while Abdul Gani had been in possession of the said land by way of purchase? he died leaving defendant No.5, Akhiluddin as his son and that while Akhiluddin had been in possession of the said land along' with other lands by amicable partition with the other co-sharers, he mutated his name in respect of .33 acre of land of suit plot No. 183 and joma was separated in Khatian No. 156; that while Akhiluddin had been in possession of the said .land he mortgaged the said property on 21-11-1991 to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 through mortgage deed No. 5569 dated 21-11-1991 and received huge loan; he also executed a power of attorney on the same date vide deed No. 5572; that plaintiffs had no right, title and possession over the suit property; that the alleged title deeds of the plaintiffs are all false and collusive; that Akhiluddin had no co-sharer in his 0.33 acre of land; that Akhiluddin defendant No. 5 as son of Abdul Gani never transferred any land to plaintiffs or their predecessors; that plaintiffs in collusion with defendant Nos. 3-5 instituted this false suit to get rid of the debt of the bank; that plaintiffs' suit is hit by principle of res- judicata as because plaintiffs previously filed Misc. Case No. 17 of 2002 in respect of self-same property before the Artha Rin Adalat; Narayangonj which was rejected on 26-10-2002 and that for the self- same matter which was finally decided by the Court on 26-10-2002, the present suit for the same relief is not maintainable; that the suit is barred under section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and that the same is liable to be dismissed.

7. The learned Joint District Judge on consideration of the pleadings of the parties framed as many as 4 issues in the suit. The documents filed by the plaintiff-appellants have been marked as Exhibit 1 to 11 and the documents filed by the defendants have been marked as Exhibit ka-cha in the suit. The plaintiffs examined 7 PWs while the defendants examined 1 DW in support of their respective cases.

8. The learned Joint District Judge by the impugned judgment and decree dated 25-2-2007 dismissed the suit mainly on the ground that the suit is barred by principle of res-judicata.

9. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred this appeal.

10. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of plaintiff-appellants has submitted that the suit is not barred by res-judicata as much as the plaintiffs instituted the suit praying for his title in the suit property arid that the miscellaneous case filed by the plaintiffs under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure only for releasing the suit property from attachment and, as such, the suit is not barred by res-judicata. He referred the case of Yunus Mia vs Bangladesh Krishi Bank reported in 54 DLR 123 and the case of Mir Laik Ali vs Standard Vacuum Oil Company (ESSO) and Abdur Razzak reported in 16 DLR 287. He also has submitted that section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is not a bar in bringing fresh suit by a 3rd party who was neither a mortgagor nor a loanee nor a guarantor. In support of this submission he referred the case of Jalaluddin Ahmed vs Md Selim Hossain reported in VII ADC 291 and the case of Dhulabhai vs State of Madhya Pradesh reported in AIR 1969 (SC) 78. He further has submitted that due to omission of rule 63 of Order XXI of the CPC the right to bring a fresh suit for declaration of plaintiff's title after rejection of the application under Order XXI, rule 61 of the Code of Civil Procedure has not been taken away. In support of his submission he relied on the case of Shoe Narain Sahuvs Lakkan Sahu reported in AIR-1945 (Patna) 434. He thereafter has submitted that defendant-respondent No. 5 who alleged to have mortgaged the property to defendant No. 1 had no right, title, possession and interest in the suit property to mortgage the same as security of the loan and that the title documents filed by the defendant No. 5 in support of his right, title and interest in the suit property were all false, forged and fabricated documents, in such circumstances the learned Judge committed illegality in not setting aside the auction declaring plaintiff's right and title in the suit property. He lastly has submitted that plaintiff-appellants having succeeded to prove their right, title, interest and possession in the suit property by adducing oral and documentary evidence, the learned Joint District Judge is wholly wrong in not decreeing the suit.

11. Plaintiff No.2, Kazi Rokon Ahmed has been examined as PW No.1. He stated that the other plaintiffs are his mother, brothers and sisters. The suit is for 0.32 acre of land of CS Plot No. 183 corresponding to RS Plot No. 259 of Mouza -Khanpur, The suit land originally belonged to Manu-who had sold 0.37 decimal land of suit plot No. 183 to Abdul Gani and others. This witness narrated the statement of the plaint as it is. In his cross-examination he stated that he is deposing on behalf of all the PW s on the strength of a power of attorney. He heard that defendant No.5 mortgaged the suit property to defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Due to non payment of loan money, defendant bank obtained decree from Artha Rin Adalat. It is not correct that due to their defeat in Misc. Case No. 17 of 2002 they lost their right to establish title. It is not correct that the suit is barred under section 20 of the Artha Rain Adalat Ain. Akhiluddin instituted partition suit in 1996 and in that suit defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were not impleaded as party. It is not correct that defendant No.5 in collusion with the plaintiffs instituted the partition suit without impleading the bank.

12. PW 2, Md Shamsuddin is an employee of the Sub-Registry Office. He proved the certified copies of some deeds.

13. PW 3, Milon Mia son of Iman Ali stated that his father Iman Ali sold out the suit land to different persons by several deeds. He had transferred 0.32 acre of land through 6 registered deeds and those deeds have been marked as Exhibit 1 series. The witness and his father used to cultivate the said land. Renu Begum (plaintiff No. 8) is one of the purchaser. All the purchasers are in possession of their purchased land. In his cross-examination he stated that his father' purchased 0.32 acre of land from Shahbuddin Sarker. He could not say whether the SA record was prepared in the name of his father with respect to that 0.32 acre of land. Thereafter he said that the SA and RS record may be prepared in the name of his father. He was present at the time of execution of those 6 deeds and that at that time he was about 25/26 years old. Those 6 deeds were registered in the year 1981 and 1982. He identified his father's signature in those deeds.

14. PW 4, Md Mofiz Uddin stated that plaintiffs, defendants and the suit land were known to him. There are trees and houses on the suit land. Those trees and the houses are standing therein since 1988. Except plaintiffs he saw none to possess the suit land. Me could not say the plot and khatian number of the suit property.

15. PW 5, Anwar Uddin Mia stated that plaintiffs purchased deed dated 28-12-1988,28-12-1988 and 18-3-1991 Ext 1(Ja), 1(Jha) and 1(Neo) he was an attesting witness. He identified his signature on those deeds and that the consideration money was paid in presence of him. In his cross-examination he denied the suggestion that those 3 deeds are forged and collusive.

16. PW 6, M. Amin Uddin stated that he was an attesting witness in the plaintiffs' two purchased deeds dated 5-7-1986 Exhibit 1, (cha) and l(chha) and that at the time of execution of the deed and payment of consideration money he was present there. He further stated that the vendor of those deeds had acquired title in the said property by purchase. They were not co-sharers in the suit jote.

17. PW 7, Md Arifur Rahman is Assistant land Officer. He stated that as per direction of the Court dated 4-7-2006 he prepared a report and submitted the same to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) and the Assistant Commissioner (Land) sent the report to the Court on 19-7-2006. He proved the report Exhibit 8. The Court asked for a report to ascertain as to whether the suit land was mutated in the name of Akhiluddin or not. The Assistant Commissioner asked him to submit the report. On the basis of a mutation he mentioned the name of different persons in his report. He denied the suggestion that he illegally mutated the name of those persons.

18. DW 1, Bimal Chandra Shaha is a Principal Officer, Rupali Bank Ltd., SK Road Branch, Narayangonj. He deposed on behalf of defendant Nos. 1 and 2. He stated that 0.37 acre of land of suit plot No. 183 originally belonged to Manu. Abdul Gani purchased the same from Manu and that defendant No.5 Akhiluddin is the son of Gani. Abdul Gani got the suit land by amicable partition among the co-sharers. Thereafter he separated khatian and mutated the suit land in his name vide Mutation Case No. 156/2. Mutation khatian has been marked as Exhibit Ka, OCR has been marked as Exhibit Kha, rent receipts has been marked as Exhibit Ga. Defendant took loan from Rupali Bank Ltd. SK Road Branch, Narayangonj. Defendant No.5, Akhiluddin was the guarantor of that loan. Against the said loan defendant No. 5 mortgaged the suit property in favour of defendant No. 1 vide mortgage deed No. 5569 dated 21-11-1991 and on the same date also registered a power of attorney vide No. 5572. Those two deeds filed and marked as Exhibit Gha and Uma. M/s Sundarban Trading did not repay the loan and, as such, obtained a decree against Akhiluddin and other defendants in Artha Rin Suit No. 59 of 1993. Photocopy of the judgment and decree of Artha Rin Suit have been marked as Exhibit Cha and Cha(1). Thereafter they filed Money Execution Case No. 44 of 2001. In that execution case plaintiffs filed a miscellaneous case being Misc. Case No. 17 of 2002 which was dismissed on contest on 26-10-2002. The certified copy of the judgment and order dated 26-10-2002 passed in Misc. Case No. 17 of 2002 has been filed and marked as Exhibit Chha. After disposal of the said miscellaneous case plaintiffs did not move the higher Court. Plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit property. Akhiluddin never sold the suit property to anyone. Plaintiffs' claim is false. He denied that plaintiffs purchased the suit property from the sons and daughters of Akhi1uddin and that except Akhiluddin none had any right to sell the suit properly. Plaintiffs' rent receipts, khatian and all other documents are collusive and ineffective. Plaintiffs instituted the suit in collusion with defendant No.5 for misappropriating the defendants money. In his cross-examination he stated that they took legal advice from their lawyer as regards the mortgage deeds and power of attorney. The suit land was amicablely partitioned among the heirs of Abdul Gani. He could not say the date and year of amicable partition. He could not say whether the name of Akhiluddin was recorded in SA khatian or not. He also stated that the mutation parcha filed by them in the name of Akhiluddin is forged. Before granting loan he personally visited the suit land. It is not correct that since 1985-86 plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit property by constructing houses and planting trees and that they took electricity connection in the suit land. He denied the suggestion that defendant No.3 in collusion with the bank officials created the power of attorney in the name of Akhiluddin who had no right, title and interest in the suit land. It is not correct that defendant No.5 as grantor had no authority to create mortgage deed and power of attorney in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and that those power of attorney and mortgage deed are collusive and forged or that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have not acquired any right and title in the suit property on the basis of those power of attorney and mortgage deed. He could not say whether 3 sons of Abdul Gani and his brother Ali Hossain had transferred 0.37 acre of land of plot No. 183 to one Shahbuddin through registered deed No. 1950 dated 8-3-1963. He further could not say whether or not Shahbuddin transferred the said land to Iman Ali and his sister Gedi Bibi vide registered deed No. 2696 dated 7-5-1965 and that after the death of Gedi Bibiher brother Iman Ali inherited her property. He also failed to say whether the land of RS Plot No. 259 of RS Khatian No. 51 was prepared in the name of Iman Ali He also could not say whether plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit property by purchasing the same through different deeds of different dates since 1981-88 from the heirs of Iman Ali and they have been living therein by constructing houses.

19. It appears from the genealogy of the plaint and written statement that Manu was the owner of 1.88 acres of land including the suit land of CS Khatian No. 96. Thereafter he had died leaving 2 sons namely Abdul Kader and Kudrat Ullah and only daughter Hayatun Bewa. Abdul Kader became owner of 0.752 acre of land including the suit land. Thereafter he died leaving 2 sons, Abdul Gani and Ali Hossain who inherited the property of their father Abdul Kader. Hay tun Bewa had transferred her 0.376 acre of land through registered deed being No. 1162 dated 31-1-1946 (Exhibit 1 Ta) to Abdul Gani and Ali Hossain. While Abdul Gani and Ali' Hossain had been in possession of their inherited and purchased land, Abdul Gani died leaving 5 sons and 3 daughters named Mobarak Hossain, Asrafuddin, Nuruddin, Shafiuddin and defendant No.5, Akhiluddin and 3 daughters were Sahera Begum, Jahanara Begum and Hena Begum. Thereafter 3 sons of Abdul Gani namely Mobarak Hossain, Asrafuddin Ahmed and Nuruddin Ahmed and their uncle Ali Hossain had transferred 0.37 acre of land of suit plot along with some other non suited lands of that khatian to Shahbuddin vide kabala deed No. 1950 dated 8-3-1963 (Exhibit 1 Tha). While Shahabuddin Mia had 'been in possession of said 0.37 acre of land of Plot No. 183 he had transferred the same to one Iman Ali and his sister Gedi Bibi vide deed No. 2696 date 7-5-1965 (Exhibit 1). Gedi Bibi died leaving her brother Iman Aliand Iman Ali became the owner of entire 0.37 acre ofland of plot No. 183 and his name was prepared in RS Khatian No. 51 of RS Plot No. 259. The said RS khatian has been filed and marked as Exhibit 2. Thereafter Iman Ali transferred 0.32 acre of land to the predecessor -in- interest of the plaintiff Nos. 1-7 and 8 vide eight (8) registered sale deeds and those deeds have been filed and marked as Exhibit 1 (Ka) to l(Neo). Plaintiffs mutated their names and have been paying rents. The mutation khatian has been field and marked as Exhibit 3 (cha), 3 (Chha), 3(Uma) and Exhibit 11. The rent receipts have been filed and marked as Exhibit 3-3 (Tha), 9 and 9(Ka) CS and RS Khatian have been filed and marked as Exhibit 2(ka)- 2(Uma). Accordingly plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land by constructing houses digging ponds and also by installing electricity and gas line in their own names. The gas bills and electricity bills have been filed and marked as Exhibit 4 and 5 series respectively.

20. The defendants claim that defendant No. 5 Akhiluddin, son of Abdul Gani had acquired the property by an amicable settlement among the co-sharers. A mutation khatian showing mutation in the name of Akhiluddin has been filed and marked as Exhibit Ka. There is no dispute between the parties as regards genealogy. It is admitted by the plaintiffs that defendant No.5, Akhiluddin is the son of Abdul Gani. Defendants further claim that defendant No.5 being owner of the suit property mortgaged the same through registered mortgage deed No. 5569 dated 21-11-1991 and that he also executed and registered a power of attorney on the same date being deed No. 5572. The mutation khatian No. 156 Exhibit ka is a genuine document. The DW 1 in his cross examination admitted that he could not say whether or not SA khatian was prepared in the name of Akhiluddin and that the mutation parcha submitted by them in the name of Akhiluddin is a forged document নালিশী এস এ খতিয়ানে অখিল উদ্দিনের নাম আছে কিনা জানিনা। অখিল উদ্দিনের নামীয় মিউটেশন পরচা (আমাদের দাখিলী ) জল। "PW7, Md Arifur Rahman, Assistant land Officer, Fatullah Union Land Office, stated that in connection with register-2 he submitted a report to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) who was directed by the Court to submit a report. The Report has been filed and marked as Exhibit 8. In that report PW 7 clearly stated that সূত্রস্থ স্বারককে বর্ণিত ১৮৫০/৯১ নং তাং ২২-৬-৯১ নামজারী জমাভাগ মোকদ্দমা মূলে বর্ণিত ১৪৮৪ নং খতিয়ানে জনাব অখিল উদ্দিন আহাম্মাদ, পিতা–মৃত-আব্দুল গনি এর নাম কোন খতিয়ান পাওয়া যায়না। From the said report Exhibit 8 it further appears that the name of Akhiluddin was not appeared in SA and RS khatian.

21. By amending the plaint plaintiffs stated that Akhiluddin and 7 others instituted a suit being Partition Suit No. 23 of 1996 for partition of their entire 1.88 acres of land of CS khatian No. 96 claiming their Saham in 0.0766 acre of land. The said suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 11 of 2001 and the same was dismissed for default on 27- 3-2003. The certified copy of the judgment and decree has been marked as Exhibit 6(kha). The plaint of that suit has been filed and marked as Exhibit 6(ga).

22. From the documents and the evidence of the parties it appears that Akhiluddin had not acquired any right, title and possession in the land of suit plot No. 183. Already we have found that no mutation khatian was prepared in the name of Akhiluddin. His mutation khatian Exhibit ka is a fabricated document. Even SA and RS khatian was not prepared in his name and the same clearly shows that he had no right, title, interest and possession in Suit Plot No. 183 corresponding to RS Plot No. 259: The P.Ws. were not cross-examined as regards possession of Akhiluddin in the suit property. The statement of PWs as regards possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property were not cross-examined. Even the DW 1 also did not deny the possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property. So, conclusion can be drawn that defendant No. 5 mortgaged the property to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 as security of the loan of defendant Nos. 3 and 4 without having any right, title, interest and possession of the suit property. On the other hand the documents filed by the plaintiffs and the evidence and materials on record clearly show that plaintiffs have right, title, interest and possession in the suit property.

23. The trial Court dismissed the suit on point of res-judicata which is required to be considered. The trial court held that plaintiffs did not take any step before the higher Court against the order dated 26- 10-2002 passed by the Court rejecting plaintiffs' Misc. Case No. 17 of 2002 filed under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure and relief claimed for the self-same property by instituting the present suit was barred by principle of res-judicata. In the Misc. Case No. 17 of 2002 the court found that plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit property, they are not entitled to get a decree cancelling the deeds mentioned in kha schedule of the plaint and the judgment and decree passed in Artha kin Suit No. 59 of 1993 as void.

24. In an application under Order XXI, rule 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Court investigate in to the matter and if satisfied that for the reason stated in the claim or objection such property was not, when attached, in the possession of the judgment-debtor or of some persons in trust for him, or in the occupancy of a tenant or other person paying rent to him, or that, being in the possession of the judgment-debtor at such time, it was so in his possession, not on his own property, but on account of or in trust for some other person, or partly on his own account and partly on account of some other person, the Court shall make an order releasing the property, wholly or to such extent as it thinks fit, from attachment. Rule .61 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure reads as under:

"61. Where the Court is satisfied that the property was, at the time it was attached, in the possession of the judgment-debtor as his own property and not on account of any other person, or was in the possession of some other per- son in trust for him, or in the occupancy of a tenant or other person paying rent to him, the Court shall disallow the claim."

25. From the averments of the rules 60 and 61 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure it appears that those two rules are (in) relating to possession of the parties which is investigated by the Court. There is no scope for deciding the title of the parties by disposing of an application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

26. In the case of Mir Laik Ali vs Standard Vacuum Oil Company (ESSO) and Abdur Razzak reported in 16 DLR 287, their lordships observed in paragraph No. 13:

...... "There can be little doubt on a perusal of those provisions that the only inquiry that affects the decision is the enquiry for ascertainment of possession. Title may have a bearing on the question of possession and for that purpose may be relevant, but an inquiry into title as such is of no avail. "

27. 'In another case of Yunus Mia (Md) vs Bangladesh Krishi Bank reported in 54 DLR 123.

The court took the same view and held that there is no doubt that:

"The scope of enquiry under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure is very limited, which is confined to the question of possession. But such possession must be independent of the judgment-debtor and .not through the judgment-debtor within the meaning of rule 61."

28. In the' case in hand the Court in' disposing' of the application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure did not examine any witness to investigate the matter for his satisfaction who is in .actual possession of the suit property. The appellants do not claim the suit property through the judgment debtor. It also appears that plaintiff-appellants are neither mortgagor nor loanee nor the guarantor and judgment-debtor of the suit property.

29. According, to defendant-bank the suit property was mortgaged to the bank by a person namely Akhiluddin Ahmed (defendant No.5) who had right, title, interest and possession in the suit property. The learned judge only came to a finding in the Misc. Case No. 170-2002 that the petitioner (plaintiff) did not mention in' their application that grantor Akhiluddin was a son of Abdul Gani and that appellants failed to establish their 'claim by any documentary evidence. The Court did not discuss the point of possession of the parties.

30. "Rule 63 of Order' XXI was, omitted by ordinance No. 48 of 1983 dated 5-9-1983. By that rule a claimant who raised objection 'as against whom an order is made rejecting his claim had right to institute a suit to establish the right' which he claims to the property in dispute: After omission of the said 'provision the person whose claim was rejected has no forum to establish his title. Section-9 of the Code of Civil Procedure has given right to a person to bring a suit to establish his right or title' in any property or thing. By deleting rule 63 of Order XXI the right of institution of a suit for title under section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure has not been taken away. The section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure reads as follows:

"9. The Courts shall (subject to the provisions herein contained) have jurisdiction to try all suits of a civil nature excepting suits of which their cognizance is either expressly or impliedly barred:"

31. This provision does not show that after deleting rule 63 of Order XXI the right to institute a fresh suit for establishing title have been expressly or impliedly made barred.

32. The learned Advocate for the appellants referred the case of Shea Narain Sahu vs Lakhan Sahu reported in AIR 1945 (Patna)' 434. A Division Bench held that:

...... "It may be taken that decision rejecting the application under Order XXI, rule 58 became final and the order was, therefore, conclusive under Order XXI, rule 63 as it is not the case of the plaintiff-appellants that any suit was filed to establish the plaintiffs' right within one year"

33. In that case further it has been held that:

"the decision or the rejection of that application, therefore, will not bar the plaintiff-appellants' present suit which is based on a title which is independent of any thing directly or indirectly decided by the rejection of the application under Order XXI, rule 58, Civil Procedure Code."

Rule 63 provided for instituting a suit by a party against whom an order is made under. 61 or 62 to establish his right and further provided that subject to the result of the suit the order passed under rules 61 or 62 would be conclusive. Rule 63 was repealed by Ordinance XLVIII of 1983, but such repeal has no effect of precluding a party from filing a regular suit to establish his right."

34. From above provisions of law we find that the present suit, after disposal of the application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not barred and section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure empowered the plaintiff to bring a suit for establishing his title, thus the suit is not barred by principle of res-judicata. So, the dismissal of the suit by the trial Court holding that the suit is barred by res-judicata is not tenable and the said suit is maintainable. Now the point is whether in view of section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 and section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the plaintiff-appellants are entitled to get a decree declaring that the judgment and decree passed by the Arth Rin-Adalat is void and collusive. Section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 provides that:

৬. অর্থঋণ আদালতের সিদ্ধান্ত চুড়ান্ত-(১) ধারা ৭ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে অর্থ ঋণ আদালতের কার্যাধারা, আদেশ রায় ও ডিক্রি সম্পর্কে কোন আদালত বা অন্য কোন কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট প্রশ্ন উত্থান করা যাইবেনা।

(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এ যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, কোন অর্থঋণ আদালত কর্তৃক বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে প্রদত্ত কোন এক তরফা ডিক্রি রদ করার জন্য বিবাদী Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908)এর Order IX এর Rule 13 এর বিধান মোতাবেক আদালতে দরখাস্ত করিতে চাহিলে তাহাকে তাহার বিরূদ্ধে ডিক্রিকৃত অর্থের অন্তত: অর্ধেক বা উহার সমপরিমান অর্থের ব্যাংক জামানত দরখাস্তের সহিত আদালতে জমা করিতে হইবে এবং উক্তরূপ জমা করা না হইলে তাহার দরখাস্ত গ্রহণযোগ্য হইবেনা।

35. Section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 provided for preferring appeal is as follows:

৭।আপীল ।-(১) কোন ব্যক্তি অর্থঋণ আদালতের কোন রায় বা ডিক্রি দ্বারা ক্ষুদ্র হইলে তিনি উক্ত রায় বা ডিক্রি প্রদানের তারিখ হইতে ৩০ দিনের মধ্যে হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে আপীল করিতে পারিবেন।

<u>36. It appears that under section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 an aggrieved party could bring an appeal on depositing 50% of the decreetal amount. However, in many decisions of our Court including Apex Court it has been decided that a person who is aggrieved by the decree of a Artha Rin Suit, may bring a fresh suit who is neither a mortgagor, nor guarantor nor a judgment-debtor.</u>

37. The provision of section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 provides as under:

ধারা ২০। অর্থঋণ আদালতের আদেশের চুড়ান্ততা ----এই আইনের বিধান ব্যতিরেকে, কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন কোন কার্য বা উহার কোন আদেশ রায় বা ডিক্রির বিষয়ে কোন প্রশ্ন উত্থাপন করা যাইবেনা, এবং আইনের বিধানকে উপেক্ষা করিয়া কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট আবেদন করিয়া কোন প্রতিকার দাবী বা প্রার্থণা করা হইলে, এরুপ আবেদন কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষ গ্রাহ্য করিবেনা।

<u>38. Under section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 an aggrieved party cannot bring a fresh suit against the decision of the Artha Rin Adalat. The section provides that no person can challenge the order or judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat under any other law except the Arth Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. If any prayer is made under any other law except the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the same shall not be entertainable.</u>

<u>39. Admittedly .the appellants are neither a mortgagor nor a loanee and nor a guarantor. Already we have found that appellants have got right, title, interest and possession in the suit property and that Akhiluddin who mortgaged the property to the bank, had no right, title and interest in the suit property. In such a position the plaintiff-appellants had no way to redress his grievances to protect his right and title of the suit property. If an ex-parte decree is passed under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the judgment-debtor can file an application under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 within 30 days from the date of decree for setting aside the said decree by depositing 10% of the decreetal amount. The judgment debtor also may file an appeal under section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 by depositing 50% of the decreetal amount within 60 days from the date of decree. But the 3rd party like the' present appellants can lodge claim under section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 according to the provisions of Civil Procedure Code by filing an application in the execution case arisen out of a decree or an order of the Artha Rin Adalat on depositing 25% of the decreetal amount.</u>

40. After rejection of an application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure the petitioner can establish his right by instituting a fresh suit under section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. As per provision of section 32 this appellant filed an application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But we do not find any relief for the appellants under the Artha-Rin-Adalat Ain after rejection of their claim which arose from the judgment and decree of the Artha Rain Adalat.

41. Similar point was decided in the case of Jalaluddin Ahmed vs Md Selim Hossain reported in 7 ADC 291. In that case it was argued before the Appellate Division that since the petitioners were the 3rd party claimants they were not required to deposit 25% of the decreetal amount in view of section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Our Appellate Division held. that the petitioners were required to deposit 25% of the decreetal amount while making an application for restoration of possession and in that view of the matter, the learned Judge of the High Court Division had committed no error in law in interfering with the judgment of the learned District Judge. The court further held that since the petitioners are not claiming title through, the judgment-debtor, this judgment will not stand on the way if they file a fresh suit for recovery of the suit property.

42. Similar point had appeared before the Supreme Court of India in the Case of Dhulabhai vs State of Madhya Pradesh reported in AIR 1969 (SC) 78, Considering the views of a special Bench who inquired into the matter and the result of the inquiry into the diverse views expressed before the court which stated as under:

"(I) Where the statute gives finality to the orders of the special tribunals the civil court's

jurisdiction must be held to be excluded if there is adequate remedy. to do what the civil court would normally- do in a suit Such provision, however, does not exclude those cases where the provisions of the particular Act have not been complied with or the statutory tribunal has not acted in conformity with the fundamental principles of judicial procedure.

(2) Where there is an express bar of the jurisdiction of the court, an examination of the scheme of the particular Act to find the adequacy or the sufficiency of the remedies provided, may be relevant but.is not decisive to sustain the jurisdiction of the civil court.

Where there is no express exclusion the examination of the remedies and the scheme of the particular Act to find out the intendment becomes necessary and the result of the inquiry may be decisive. In the hitter case it is necessary to see if the statute creates a special right or a liability and provides for the determination of the right or liability and further lays down that all questions about the said right and liability shall 'be determined by the tribunals so constituted, and whether remedies normally associated with action in civil courts are prescribed by the said statute not."

43. In another case of Al Baraka Bank Bangladesh Ltd. Vs Rina Alam reported in 56 DLR 588. A Division Bench of this Court held that:

"Jurisdiction of Artha Rin Adalat was created with particular objective, mainly for recovery of bank dues. To achieve the purpose, Artha Rin Adalat was made deemed to be a civil court but not a full-fledged civil court with all powers and jurisdiction of a civil court. It is a civil court of defined and limited jurisdiction."

<u>44. In the present case all the deeds in respect of the suit property of the plaintiff-appellants are in possession of the 'plaintiff-appellants. They filed those title deeds from their possession and the same were marked as exhibits, they have mutated their names and SA and RS records were prepared in the name of the predecessor and predecessor in interest of the plaintiffs. The reason who mortgaged the suit property to the defendant-bank (defendant No.5) had no right, title, interest and possession of the suit property. The mutation parch a filed by the defendant-respondent No.5 in the earlier Artha Rin Adalat in support of his title has been found forged and fabricated documents and the DW No.1 has admitted that the mutation parcha filed by Akhiluddin at the time of obtaining loan is a forged document. An employee of the Registry Office has been examined in this case who deposed before the Court showing the volume of register. On examination of the volume the it is found that there is no existence of any mutation parcha in' the volume. In such circumstances, the plaintiff-appellants who have actual right, title and possession of the suit property is entitled to a decree declaring their title in the suit property. The above cited law reports show that the plaintiffs' suit was maintainable and the plaintiffs succeeded to prove that they have right, title and interest in the suit property. The learned Judge dismissed the suit only on the ground that the suit is barred by principle of res-judicata but we find from all the evidence and materials on record that the suit should be decided on merit. In such circumstances, it appears to us that no fruitful purpose will be served if the suit is remanded for deciding the suit on merit. All the evidence and material on record speak that plaintiffs have right, title and possession in the suit property. Thus we find substance in this appeal.</u>

45. In the result the appeal is allowed without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree dated 25-2-2007 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court; Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 163 of 2002 dismissing the suit is hereby set aside and the suit is decreed and plaintiffs' title is declared in the suit property. The preliminary decree dated 27-9-2000 and final decree dated 25-3-2001 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat Narayanganj in Artha Rin Suit No59 of 1993 is illegal, collusive, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff-appellants.

Send down the lower court records.

End.
